### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, five activities — A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 — each ran in roughly 17–24 in 100 traces, around the middle of the trace; in the later window each appears in at most about 1 in 100 traces, and A26 is not observed at all (0 of 200 traces). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, POS003, POS005, POS006]
- In the earlier window A29 and A30 fed this block: about 5–9 in 100 of A29's outgoing transitions went to each block member and about 6–15 in 100 of A30's, and the members in turn led mainly to A31 (about 58–68 in 100) or back to A30 (about 29–40 in 100). In the later window, A29 leads to A30 in about 97 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions and A30 leads to A31 in about 98 in 100. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- The new direct route is also tighter in steps: A29 is followed by A30 within one step in about 96 in 100 cases (previously about 60), A30 is followed by A31 within one step in about 99 in 100 (previously about 38, with most of the rest two steps away), A29 reaches A31 typically two steps later instead of three, and A31 itself now appears slightly earlier in the trace (mean position about 0.54 versus about 0.57). [LAG014, LAG017, LAG015, POS007]
- Adjacencies that bridged the block largely vanish: A29→A20, A29→A25, A20→A31 and A30→A25 were each observed in about 25–46 traces before and in at most one trace after. [LAG005, LAG011, LAG012, LAG016]
- Co-occurrence mirrors this: A20 and A27 each occurred together with A14, A15, A28, A29, A30, A31 or A43 in about 23–24 in 100 traces before and in about 1 in 100 after, and block-internal pairs such as A20–A25 or A25–A26 are now seen together in essentially no trace. [REL014, REL016, REL021, REL024, REL030, REL033, REL018, REL026]
- Separately, A04 became far more prominent: it runs in about 63 in 100 traces in the later window (about 20 in 100 before) and now sits late in the trace (median position about 0.89 versus about 0.34); A14, A28, A29, A30, A31 and A43 each precede A04 in about 55–56 in 100 of the traces where both occur, whereas before the two co-occurred in only about 21 in 100 traces with mixed or absent order. [OCC002, POS001, REL001, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]
- A04's connections changed accordingly: A46 now sends about 68 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A04 (about 5 in 100 before, when about 81 in 100 went to A47), A04 leads to A47 in about 88 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 17 in 100 before, spread over many successors), and A47 is followed by A04 typically three steps later (33 traces, against 8 before). [DIR011, DIR001, LAG021, LAG023, REL013]
- Smaller shifts: participation in A02, A06 and A10 fell to about 5–7 in 100 traces (from about 17–21); A28 reaches A31 five steps later in about 180 of 200 traces (one observation before); and several edges became near-exclusive (A14→A15 about 85→98 in 100, A15→A16 about 93→98 in 100, A43→A28 about 80→93 in 100). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, LAG010, DIR002, DIR003, DIR010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the process skips the block of five alternative activities A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 that previously ran between A29/A30 and A31: the block's participation collapsed from roughly 17–24 in 100 traces to at most about 1 in 100 (A26 unobserved), the transitions from A29 and A30 into the block disappeared, and flow now passes from A29 to A30 and from A30 to A31 in about 97 and 98 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions, typically one step apart. The screening context fits a real change rather than sampling noise — 87 control-flow items qualified where about 1 would be expected without a change — and the occurrence, routing, co-occurrence and step-distance indicators all describe this same block consistently. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, DIR008, DIR009, LAG014, LAG017, REL014, REL018]

What the evidence cannot rule out is that the block still exists but was rarely taken in this particular sample: A19, A20, A25 and A27 still appear in 1–2 after-window traces, and the later-window routing profiles of A20, A25 and A27 rest on only 1–2 observations, so a full removal and a rarely-triggered optional block look the same here. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC009, DIR004, DIR005, DIR007]

Other differences: A04, A46 and A47 form a separate change — A04 now runs in about 63 in 100 traces near the end of the trace (previously about 20 in 100, earlier and with mixed successors), is entered from A46 (about 68 in 100 of A46's outgoing transitions, previously about 5) and leads on to A47 (about 88 in 100, previously about 17). Participation in A02, A06 and A10 also fell to about 5–7 in 100 traces, and several edges became near-exclusive (A14→A15, A15→A16, A43→A28). [OCC002, POS001, REL001, REL007, DIR011, DIR001, LAG021, LAG023, REL013, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR002, DIR003, DIR010]
